study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective randomized controlled trial
exposure: short transvaginal ultrasound cervical length (TVU CL)
cohort: Asymptomatic singleton pregnancies without prior spontaneous preterm birth (SPTB) but with TVU CL ≤ 25 mm at 18 0/6-23 6/7 weeks
finding: In asymptomatic singleton pregnancies with short cervix, performing exercise ≥2 days a week for ≥20 min each day was not associated with an increased risk of PTB < 37 weeks.
mod_finding: In asymptomatic singleton pregnancies with short cervix, performing exercise ≥2 days a week for ≥20 min each day does not increase the risk of preterm birth.
